**ALUNA: An Immersive 3D Space Exploration and Autonomous Satellite Operations Game**

ALUNA is an interactive, space-themed 3D platform developed to make space exploration and satellite operations more engaging, accessible, and educational. It combines an immersive 3D space headquarters, mission-based gameplay, spacecraft design, satellite fleet management, and autonomous intelligence systems. The platform features 25 solo campaign levels, 25 squad campaign levels, and four multiplayer modes, encouraging both individual learning and teamwork.

ALUNA addresses the challenge by transforming complex space concepts into interactive missions and simulations. Players can explore different facilities, coordinate with teammates, manage spacecraft and satellites, and experience scenarios inspired by real-world space operations. Its autonomous systems aim to help users understand satellite coordination, orbital safety, and potential close-approach risks.

The project is important because satellites support communication, navigation, weather forecasting, and scientific research. As space becomes increasingly crowded, understanding responsible satellite operations and orbital safety is essential. ALUNA makes these topics more approachable while inspiring interest in space science, technology, and future space exploration.
details:
ALUNA – Project Details

ALUNA is an immersive 3D space exploration and autonomous satellite operations platform that combines gaming, space science, simulation, and teamwork. It is designed to help users understand space missions and the challenges of managing satellites through interactive experiences.

1. What does it do and how does it work?

ALUNA features an interactive 3D space headquarters that acts as the central hub. Users can explore different facilities, including Mission Control, Satellite Operations, Spacecraft Design, Autonomous Intelligence, Training and Simulation, and Squad Coordination.

The platform includes:

  • 25 Solo Campaign Levels for individual space missions.
  • 25 Squad Campaign Levels for cooperative missions.
  • 4 Multiplayer Modes to encourage teamwork and coordination.
  • Satellite Fleet Management to monitor and manage satellite operations.
  • Orbital Safety Simulation to understand satellite close approaches and collision risks.
  • Autonomous Intelligence Systems to support monitoring, decision-making, and mission coordination.
  • Spacecraft Design and Mission Planning to make space operations interactive.

Players navigate a 3D environment, enter facilities, select missions, operate spacecraft, and collaborate with teammates to complete objectives.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Makes complex space science concepts easier to understand.
  • Encourages STEM learning through interactive gameplay.
  • Builds teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Introduces satellite management and orbital safety concepts.
  • Promotes awareness of responsible space operations.
  • Makes learning about space more engaging and accessible.

3. What is the intended impact?

ALUNA aims to inspire students and young innovators to explore space science, aerospace engineering, satellite technology, and autonomous systems. It also highlights the importance of orbital safety and responsible satellite operations as the number of objects in Earth's orbit increases.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

The project uses modern web and 3D development technologies, including:

  • Frontend: React, JavaScript, HTML, CSS
  • 3D Environment: Three.js, React Three Fiber
  • 3D Modelling and Animation: Blender
  • Backend: Python
  • Database: SQLite
  • Simulation: Orbital simulation and satellite close-approach screening
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code and web development tools

5. How is the project creative?

ALUNA combines the immersive experience of a 3D video game with educational space simulations. Instead of presenting space concepts through ordinary text or videos, it allows users to explore a virtual space headquarters, undertake missions, manage satellite systems, and work together as a squad. Cinematic character introductions, interactive facilities, realistic space environments, and autonomous mission systems create a distinctive learning experience.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The team considered:

  • Scientific relevance: Keeping missions connected to real space-operation concepts.
  • Orbital safety: Highlighting satellite collision risks and responsible operations.
  • User experience: Making controls, navigation, and missions understandable.
  • Team collaboration: Supporting squad coordination and multiplayer interaction.
  • Performance: Optimising 3D graphics and gameplay for smooth operation.
  • Scalability: Designing the platform to support additional missions and features.
  • Accessibility: Making space education engaging for a broad audience.

Keywords: Space Exploration, Satellite Operations, Autonomous Intelligence, Orbital Mechanics, Orbital Safety, Collision Risk Detection, 3D Simulation, STEM Education, Space Technology, Mission Control, Satellite Fleet Management, Three.js, React, React Three Fiber, Blender, Python, Multiplayer Gaming, Team Collaboration, Aerospace Innovation.
